items.reasons: A provides the stronger verification procedure: it covers plugin agents and silent hooks, distinguishes listed availability from execution, and checks read-only diagnostics before asking. B’s presence-based wording can underverify disconnected MCP servers and overlooks agent-only plugins. Official documentation confirms /plugin exists; C4’s headless command list does not establish otherwise. C1–C2 support A’s conditional Skill guard and replacing the current instruction. The reported K5–K6 comparison favors A under its preregistered order: both had zero wrong statuses, but A had 10 correct versus B’s 8. K6 tied. This small, single-model headless comparison does not establish interactive performance or exercise a genuinely unresolvable fallback. B handles that unattended fallback more explicitly, but A’s coverage and observed results outweigh this limitation.
